key_insight: A green interfacial-welding strategy uses waterborne polyurethane to “stitch” silk nanofibrils into a robust hierarchical aerogel that combines thermal insulation with EMI shielding.
engineering_relevance: The approach points to lightweight protective materials for extreme environments where mechanical durability, low heat transfer, and electromagnetic protection must coexist.
method: Use waterborne polyurethane as a molecular solder at silk nanofibril contact nodes
Build multi-site hydrogen bonding and chain entanglement to form an interconnected 3D network
Add carbon nanotubes to enable electrical conduction, interfacial polarization, and EMI shielding
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ultralow density (4 mg cm−3), compressive stress of 20.1 kPa at 80% strain, thermal conductivity of 28.5 mW m−1 K−1, EMI shielding effectiveness of 40 dB, and conductivity of 139.3 S m−1.
watch_item: Performance may depend on maintaining the delicate porous architecture and uniform CNT dispersion during scale-up and under long-term environmental aging.
paper_title: Interfacial Welding Enabled Hierarchical Silk Nanofibrous Aerogels for Thermal and Electromagnetic Protection in Extreme Environments
